title: The shape of an XML row
prompt: This program writes a small XML file of invoices and reads it back. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
xml = """<invoices>
  <invoice number="INV-1">
    <status>paid</status>
    <line>40</line>
  </invoice>
  <invoice number="INV-2">
    <status>open</status>
    <line>25</line>
    <line>10</line>
  </invoice>
</invoices>
"""
with open("/tmp/c1_invoices.xml", "w") as f:
    f.write(xml)

inv = spark.read.option("rowTag", "invoice").xml("/tmp/c1_invoices.xml")
print(inv.columns)
print(inv.count())
print(dict(inv.dtypes)["line"])
hints: Each `<invoice>` element is one row. Inferred columns come out in alphabetical order.
An attribute becomes a column whose name starts with `_`.
`<line>` repeats inside INV-2, so it's an array for every row. What type do whole numbers get?
